content: NOM1, also known as Nucleolar protein with MIF4G domain 1, is a protein in humans encoded by the NOM1 gene. Proteins containing MIF4G (Middle of eIF4G) and/or MA3 domains, such as NOM1, play a role in the process of protein translation. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of NOM1. A conditional knockout mouse line, named Nom1tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a high-throughput mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. Both male and female mice from this line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 25 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and three significant abnormalities were identified. No homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and none survived to the weaning stage. Consequently, the remaining tests were performed on heterozygous mutant adult mice. Among these, female mice exhibited an abnormal hair cycle.
